title: allium monadelphum var. atrosanguineum
intro: Allium monadelphum var. atrosanguineum, commonly known as the Black Hungarian Onion, is a species of wild onion that belongs to the Allium genus. It has been used in traditional medicine for its numerous health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antiviral properties, which may help alleviate symptoms of colds, flu, and respiratory infections. The therapeutic actions of Black Hungarian Onion include expectorant and diaphoretic properties, which aid in relieving congestion and fever. The bioactive constituents of this plant include sulfur compounds, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties and potential health benefits.
